attacks.claim: go.mod adds a local-path replace pointing zap at ../zap. A clean CI checkout has no such path, so the build fails; if it resolves on a build host, the binary distributed to on-call laptops is built from unpinned, unreviewed local source. The replace also overrides the pinned pseudo-version, so the stated JSON encoder fix is not what gets built.

printPlan re-implements batching with different math than computeBatches: floor(len(hosts)*MaxSurge) over all hosts instead of ceil(len(rest)*MaxSurge) over the canary-excluded remainder. Printed batch sizes and boundaries differ from what the real rollout deploys, defeating the feature's purpose of letting on-call trust the plan.
attacks.evidence: per := int(float64(len(hosts)) * o.MaxSurge)  vs  size := int(math.Ceil(float64(len(rest)) * o.MaxSurge))

attacks.claim: With --canary set, printPlan prints the canary as batch 0 and then iterates over the full hosts slice, so the canary appears again in a later batch. The plan misstates which hosts deploy where (e.g. 10 hosts, canary a, 0.25: real [a],[b c d],... vs printed [a],[a b],...).
